1. Purpose and Scope
The package controls a demonstration liquid-transfer process consisting of two tanks, three actuated
isolation valves, two level measurements and three operator pushbuttons. The controller is expected to
execute the normal sequence automatically once started and to support pause/resume and controlled
shutdown commands.

3. Functional Requirements
URS-F-001 - START shall initiate automatic operation when the system is in its initial condition.
URS-F-002 - Normal operation shall fill Tank 1 by opening V1.
URS-F-003 - V1 shall close when Tank 1 reaches the specified high-level limit.
URS-F-004 - After a 10 s waiting period, V2 shall open and transfer liquid from Tank 1 to Tank 2.
URS-F-005 - V2 shall close when Tank 1 reaches its minimum operating level.
URS-F-006 - After a 10 s waiting period, V3 shall open and drain Tank 2.
URS-F-007 - V3 shall close when Tank 2 reaches its minimum operating level.
URS-F-008 - The automatic process shall continue cyclically unless stopped or shut down.
URS-M-001 - STOP shall close all three valves and suspend automatic operation until another operator command is
received.
URS-M-002 - START after STOP shall continue the process operation rather than force a new empty-cycle
initialization.
URS-M-003 - SHUT shall empty both tanks by opening V2 and V3 and shall inhibit V1.
URS-M-004 - When shutdown emptying is achieved, V2 and V3 shall close and the controller shall return to the start
configuration.

5. Interfaces
Level measurements LT-101 and LT-102 shall be available to PLC-101. START, STOP and SHUT are
momentary commands. Valve commands are binary open/closed outputs. The supplier shall provide
actuators that fail closed on loss of power.
6. Verification Intent
Sequence operation, stop/resume behavior and controlled shutdown shall be demonstrated in simulation.
The exact demonstration command schedule will be issued in the validation procedure.

CONTROL LOGIC DESIGN NOTE
Two-Tank Fill/Transfer/Drain Controller

This note defines the controller state semantics and resolves command-priority questions raised against URS-001 Rev A. It does not replace the mechanical model or supplier data. Numeric setpoints and delays shall follow the latest approved parameter/change records.
SHUT has the highest command priority. A valid SHUT edge immediately abandons any stored resume context and enters SHUTDOWN.
STOP has the next priority. STOP is accepted from any normal running or wait state and places the controller in PAUSED with all valve outputs false.
START has the lowest priority. START from IDLE begins FILL_T1; START from PAUSED restores the interrupted state. START while already running is ignored.
Commands received while SHUTDOWN is active do not interrupt the shutdown sequence. A new START is required after shutdown has completed and the controller has returned to IDLE.

When STOP occurs in WAIT_AFTER_FILL, WAIT_AFTER_TRANSFER or WAIT_AFTER_DRAIN, the remaining delay shall be retained. START shall resume with that remaining delay. Reinitializing the whole delay on resume was rejected in DR-02 because it makes operator stop duration affect process timing.
V1 and V2 shall never be open simultaneously.
V2 and V3 shall not be open simultaneously during normal automatic operation.
The V2/V3 simultaneous-open restriction is explicitly waived in SHUTDOWN.
All valves are de-energize-to-close. On controller power loss, output commands shall be false.
Level threshold comparisons shall include equality (>= high, <= low).

Legacy simulation code uses states FILL, HOLD1, TRANSFER, HOLD2, DRAIN and HOLD3. These map to FILL_T1, WAIT_AFTER_FILL, TRANSFER_T1_T2, WAIT_AFTER_TRANSFER, DRAIN_T2 and WAIT_AFTER_DRAIN respectively. The old code has no explicit PAUSED state object and handles STOP with a Boolean latch.
Controls tuning requested a small increase in T1 high limit above the 0.78 m URS baseline. Formal approval was pending when Rev B of this note was issued.
Post-transfer and inter-cycle delays were still under customer review at document release. Use a later approved change request if available.

location.section: DR-02 Design Review Minutes - Two-Tank Controller

content: The URS says STOP waits for either START or SHUT but does not state what happens to an active delay timer. Controls proposed freezing remaining delay. Simulation initially restarted the entire delay on resume. The review board selected **freeze remaining delay** because STOP should pause the process rather than alter the sequence timing.

The term `shut` was confirmed to mean a **controlled process shutdown/drain**, not an emergency-stop function. During SHUT, V1 must remain closed while V2 and V3 are commanded open together. This is an intentional exception to the normal prohibition on opening the transfer and drain valves together.

- **D-01:** Command precedence is `SHUT > STOP > START`.
- **D-02:** STOP closes all valves and stores the interrupted state.
- **D-03:** STOP during any delay freezes the remaining delay; START resumes the remaining delay.
- **D-04:** START while the automatic sequence is already running is ignored.
- **D-05:** START and STOP received during active SHUT are ignored.
- **D-06:** SHUT is complete only when both LT-101 and LT-102 are at or below their low-level setpoints.
- **D-07:** After shutdown completion, all valves are closed and the sequence context is reset to IDLE. A later START begins a new fill cycle.
- **D-08:** V1 and V2 must never be commanded open together.
- **D-09:** V2 and V3 must not be commanded open together in normal auto operation; SHUT is the only permitted exception.

- **A-17 / Customer:** Confirm whether T1 high should be increased from 0.78 m to 0.80 m. *Closed by CR-004 on 11 Mar 2026.*
- **A-18 / Customer:** Confirm post-transfer delay. *Closed by CR-004: 12 s.*
- **A-19 / Controls:** Consider reducing inter-cycle delay after Tank 2 low. *Closed by CR-004: 8 s.*
- **A-20 / Simulation:** Update legacy model after parameter approval. *No evidence of completion in the supplied packet.*

The final SysML representation should distinguish the operator commands (events), the controller states, the physical valve/tank parts, the hydraulic connections and the requirement/verification elements. Do not model `shut` as a power-loss or emergency-stop event.

4. Acceptance Criteria
AC-01 - T1 shall reach the effective high-level setpoint of 0.80 m before the first transfer begins.
AC-02 - All valves shall be closed throughout the STOP interval from 220 s until the START command at 280 s.
AC-03 - The START at 280 s shall resume the interrupted transfer rather than restart filling.
AC-04 - Following completion of the first T2 drain, the controller shall automatically begin another fill cycle after the
effective 8 s inter-cycle delay.
AC-05 - All valves shall be closed throughout the STOP interval from 650 s until SHUT at 700 s.
AC-06 - At 700 s V1 shall remain closed and V2/V3 shall be commanded open together for controlled draining.
AC-07 - After shutdown drain completion the controller shall return to IDLE with all valves closed and shall remain
there through 900 s because no subsequent START is scheduled.
AC-08 - Normal automatic operation shall never command V1 and V2 simultaneously, nor V2 and V3 simultaneously.
The latter combination is permitted only in SHUTDOWN.
5. Expected State Timing Guidance
Exact threshold transition timestamps depend on numerical integration and event ordering. A tolerance of
+/-2 s is acceptable for state-boundary comparisons when the effective parameter set is used. The provided
CSV is the benchmark trace generated with 1 s logging.
